synthesis: Scout cannot resend invite or re-add deleted user because users.email has a database unique constraint that INCLUDES soft-deleted rows, and Laravel validation does NOT exclude trashed users by default. Root cause: (1) migration 0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table.php line 14 creates unique(email) without a partial unique index WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (codebase KNOWS about partial indexes from kit_shifts migration); (2) ScoutUsersResource line 140 and UsersResource line 58 use ->unique('users','email') without ->whereNull('deleted_at'); (3) custom validation at ScoutUsersResource lines 154-170 queries User::where('email',…)->exists() without excluding trashed. When a Scout user is soft-deleted via UsersResource DeleteAction (line 215-218), their email remains blocked. The reporter's 'delete then re-add' workflow fails at validation even though the DB would allow INSERT if validation passed — but it wouldn't, because the unique INDEX (not just validation) includes soft-deleted rows. Resend action exists (from the earlier resend-onboarding hotfix) but only works for unverified users who haven't been deleted. Outcome: stuck Scout user cannot be re-onboarded without manual DB DELETE or restore via UsersResource RestoreAction.

scope.summary: Fix email uniqueness validation to exclude soft-deleted users in ScoutUsersResource (new_user_email, existing_user_email) and UsersResource (email). Add database migration to create partial unique index on users(email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL and drop existing full unique constraint. Enhance validation error messages to detect trashed-user collision and guide admin to restore. Document restore-then-re-enable flow. Escalate token invalidation question (AC2 interpretation).

proposed_changes.change: Replace ->unique() validation on new_user_email (line 140) with Rule::unique('users','email')->whereNull('deleted_at')->ignoreRecord(false). Add custom validation closure to detect trashed-user collision: if validation fails, query User::onlyTrashed()->where('email',…)->first() and fail with 'This email belongs to a deleted user ({name}). Please restore them in Users, then re-enable Scout access here.' Same for existing_user_email (lines 154-170).
proposed_changes.reason: Exclude soft-deleted users from uniqueness check so email can be reused after delete. Provide actionable error message naming the trashed user and available actions (restore in Users resource, then re-enable Scout in Scout Users resource).

proposed_changes.change: Replace ->unique() validation on email (lines 54-65) with Rule::unique('users','email')->whereNull('deleted_at')->ignoreRecord(true). Add similar trashed-collision detection.
proposed_changes.reason: Same issue on general Users resource create/edit flow. Email must be reusable after soft delete.

proposed_changes.change: NEW migration: (1) Drop existing unique constraint on users.email via raw SQL: ALTER TABLE users DROP CONSTRAINT users_email_unique; (2) Create partial unique index: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_email_unique_active ON users (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL; (3) Add down() that reverses: drops partial index, recreates full unique.
proposed_changes.reason: Database-level enforcement of 'email unique among non-deleted users'. Mirrors kit_shifts pattern (migration 2026_05_26_000000_create_kit_shifts_table.php lines 51-55). Without this, validation fix alone would pass but INSERT would still fail on existing full unique index.

proposed_changes.change: NEW doc: Document restore flow for deleted Scout users: (1) admin notices 'email already in use' error; (2) navigate to Users resource; (3) apply 'With Inactive Users' filter; (4) locate trashed user; (5) click Restore; (6) return to Scout Users resource; (7) re-enable Scout access / resend onboarding. Also note: resend_onboarding (line 356-412) does NOT invalidate prior URLs — both old and new remain valid until 7-day expiry. ScoutSetPasswordController guards reuse AFTER password-set via email_verified_at check (line 71-73), but before that multiple URLs coexist. Escalate to product: is overlapping-valid-links acceptable, or must prior link be cryptographically invalidated on resend?
proposed_changes.reason: Clarifies UX for admins encountering this scenario. Surfaces token-invalidation design question for AC2.

questions.q: Does the users.email database constraint include soft-deleted rows?
questions.answer: YES. Migration 0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table.php line 14: $table->string('email')->unique()->nullable(); — this is a FULL unique index with NO WHERE clause. PostgreSQL unique constraints include ALL rows regardless of deleted_at. The codebase KNOWS about partial indexes (kit_shifts migration lines 51-55 creates one for at-most-one-open-shift-per-kit), but did NOT use one for users.email.

questions.q: Would validation-only fix (whereNull deleted_at) still fail at INSERT due to DB constraint?
questions.answer: YES. Even if validation passes, PostgreSQL would reject INSERT with unique violation error because existing full unique index includes soft-deleted rows. Must drop full unique constraint and replace with partial unique index WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.
questions.source: PostgreSQL unique constraint behavior + migration analysis

questions.q: Does resend invalidate prior invite URL?
questions.answer: NO. ScoutOnboardingNotification (line 28-33) generates new temporarySignedRoute with 7-day TTL. Both old and new URLs remain valid until their respective expiry. ScoutSetPasswordController guards reuse AFTER password-set via email_verified_at (line 71-73), but BEFORE that multiple URLs coexist. This is a design question: is overlapping-valid-links acceptable, or must prior link be cryptographically invalidated?

questions.q: Can admin delete Scout user via ScoutUsersResource?
questions.answer: NO. ScoutUsersResource.canDelete() returns false (line 502-505), so no delete action in that resource. Deletion happens via UsersResource DeleteAction (line 215-218), which soft-deletes (User model uses SoftDeletes trait line 101). This is intentional separation: Users resource owns user lifecycle, Scout Users resource owns Scout permission + kit tie.

escalate.reason: AC2 interpretation: 'Fresh token invalidates prior one' — current implementation allows overlapping-valid-links (both old and new signed URLs remain valid until their respective 7-day expiry). ScoutSetPasswordController guards reuse AFTER password-set via email_verified_at, so security is not compromised, but AC2 may require cryptographic invalidation of prior URL on resend (e.g. nonce/version column, validate in guardUser). Recommend product decision: (A) accept overlapping-valid-links as sufficient (simpler, already safe), or (B) implement nonce-based invalidation (complex, strict single-use-per-resend). If (B), scope grows to include nonce column on users, validation in ScoutSetPasswordController, tests for invalidation. See the signed-URL invalid-signature precedent.
